title: Procedural Geographic Flight Routes
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that visualizes procedural geographic flight routes on a 3D globe with animated stork models flying along the routes.

## Scene Setup
- Create a sphere of radius 5 to represent Earth, textured with a procedurally generated globe (use colored segments for continents: green land masses, blue ocean). Apply a MeshPhongMaterial.
- Add an ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light (intensity 0.8) at position (10, 10, 10).
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 0, 15), looking at origin. Add OrbitControls for mouse interaction.
- Background: dark navy (0x0a0a2e).

## Flight Routes
- Define exactly 5 city nodes on the globe surface using lat/lon converted to 3D positions (radius 5.05):
  - Node 0: New York (40.7N, 74.0W)
  - Node 1: London (51.5N, 0.1W)
  - Node 2: Tokyo (35.7N, 139.7E)
  - Node 3: Sydney (33.9S, 151.2E)
  - Node 4: Cape Town (33.9S, 18.4E)
- For each city, place a small red sphere (radius 0.08) at its position. Add a text sprite label above each city.
- Create curved flight routes as QuadraticBezierCurve3 arcs between these pairs: NY-London, London-Tokyo, Tokyo-Sydney, Sydney-CapeTown, CapeTown-NY. The control point for each arc should be at 1.5x the midpoint distance from center (creating a visible arc above the globe).
- Render each route as a TubeGeometry (radius 0.02, 64 segments) with a glowing cyan material (emissive 0x00ffff).

## Stork Models
- Load the model 'stork.glb' using GLTFLoader. Clone it 5 times (one per route). Scale each stork to 0.15. Each stork animates along its assigned route using a parameter t from 0 to 1, looping continuously. Storks should orient (lookAt) their forward direction along the curve tangent.
- Animation speed: each stork completes one loop in 8 seconds. Stagger start times so stork i starts at t_offset = i * 0.2.

## UI Controls
- Add a DOM panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text) showing:
  - 'Active Routes: 5/5'
  - 'Selected Route: None'
  - 'Speed Multiplier: 1.0x'
  - 'Storks Loaded: 0/5' (updates as models load)
- Add buttons:
  - 'Toggle Route' button (id='btn-toggle'): cycles through routes 0-4 and toggles their visibility. Each click selects next route index (wrapping) and toggles that route's tube + stork visibility.
  - 'Speed Up' button (id='btn-speedup'): multiplies animation speed by 1.5 (max 4.0x)
  - 'Speed Down' button (id='btn-speeddown'): divides animation speed by 1.5 (min 0.25x)
  - 'Reset View' button (id='btn-reset'): resets camera to initial position (0,0,15)
  - 'Highlight Mode' button (id='btn-highlight'): toggles highlight mode. When active, the currently selected route pulses (opacity oscillates between 0.3 and 1.0). Button text changes to 'Highlight: ON'/'Highlight: OFF'.

## Keyboard Controls
- Press '1'-'5' keys: directly select and highlight route 0-4 (set selectedRoute to that index, update HUD).
- Press 'Space': pause/resume all stork animations.
- Press 'R': reset all routes to visible, speed to 1.0x, highlight off.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- globeRadius: 5 (constant)
- routeCount: number of total routes (5)
- activeRoutes: number of currently visible routes
- selectedRoute: index of selected route (-1 if none)
- speedMultiplier: current speed multiplier (float)
- isPaused: boolean
- highlightMode: boolean
- storksLoaded: number of stork models successfully loaded (0-5)
- storkPositions: array of 5 objects {x, y, z} for each stork's current world position
- storkT: array of 5 floats representing each stork's current t parameter (0-1)
- routeVisibility: array of 5 booleans
- cameraDistance: distance from camera to origin
- frameCount: incremented each animation frame
physics_constraints: Storks must remain on their curved paths above the globe surface at all times. Stork positions must satisfy: distance from origin >= globeRadius (5.0). Animation parameter t must always be in [0,1]. Speed multiplier clamped to [0.25, 4.0]. All stork positions must be NaN-free.
